summary_en: Harry had nothing left to do.
translation_fa: هری چیزی برای انجام نمانده بود.
verbatim_html: There was nothing left to do.

summary_en: Nothing remained to plan.
translation_fa: هیچ چیزی برای برنامه‌ریزی باقی نمانده بود.
summary_fa: برنامه‌ای برای پیش رفتن باقی نمانده بود.
verbatim_html: There was nothing left to plan.

summary_en: He had nothing left to think about.
translation_fa: چیز برای فکر کردن باقی نمانده بود.
summary_fa: فکری برای فکر کردن باقی نمانده بود.
verbatim_html: There was nothing left to think.

summary_en: The new worst memory surfaced in that emptiness.
translation_fa: در آن خالی،{yād-e} جدیدی بدترین{Yād} به سطح آمد.
verbatim_html: Into that emptiness rose the new worst memory -

summary_en: Exhausted, Harry walked toward the Great Hall, haunted by thoughts of Hermione and regret over his talks with McGonagall and his parents.
translation_fa: هری خسته از فکر به طرف سالن بزرگ رفت. ذهنّشAFKAR…
summary_fa: هری خسته به طرف سالن بزرگ رفت.
verbatim_html: The Boy-Who-Lived-Unlike-His-Best-Friend trudged the long, echoing corridors toward the Great Hall. With all his energies of thought exhausted, his mind was starting to throw out thoughts like an image of Hermione walking beside him and wordless concepts like That will never happen again until another part yelled No and shouted it down with determination to bring her back, only that part's voice was getting tired and the other part seemed tireless. Another part of his mind insisted on reviewing what he'd said to Professor McGonagall and Dad and Mum, even though he'd only been trying to get them out of there as quickly as possible and had been running on limited mental energy. As though somehow he could have done better, by an act of his defective will. What would be left of his relationship with his parents now, Harry couldn't guess.

summary_en: Harry reached a junction where an older Slytherin boy waited in green-fringed black robes.
verbatim_html:
He came finally to a junction where there waited a older boy in
green-fringed black robes, silently reading a textbook, on the path
that anyone would pick if they wanted to intercept someone going
from the healer's chambers to the Great Hall.

summary_en: Harry recognized the Slytherin boy's face while wearing his Cloak of Invisibility.
verbatim_html:
Harry was wearing the Cloak of Invisibility, of course, he'd put
it on after leaving the office, rendering himself immune to almost
all forms of magical detection. There was no point in making it
easy for anyone trying to find him and kill him. And Harry was
almost set to continue past without bothering to find out what was
going on, when he recognized the Slytherin boy's face.

summary_en: Harry realized who had been waiting for him.
verbatim_html:
Realization dawned on Harry then. Of course, one of the students
who had stayed in school over the Easter holiday would naturally
have been -

summary_en: Harry told the boy he had been waiting for him.
verbatim_html:
"You were waiting for me," Harry said out loud, without removing
the Cloak.

summary_en: The Slytherin boy jerked back and dropped his textbook.
verbatim_html:
The Slytherin boy jerked back, hitting his head against the
wall, his fifth-year Charms textbook dropping from his hands,
before he looked up with wide eyes.

summary_en: The boy started to speak, saying "You're-".
verbatim_html: "You're -"

summary_en: Harry told him to say what he meant.
verbatim_html: "Invisible. Yes. Say what you mean to say."

summary_en: Lesath Lestrange asked if he had done the right thing by not stepping forward.
verbatim_html:
Lesath Lestrange scrambled to his feet, a position of attention,
then blurted out, "My lord, did I do the right thing - I thought
you would not wish me to step forward before all those others, that
they might suspect our connection - I thought, surely if you wished
my help you would call on me -"

summary_en: Harry reflected on how many ways he could kill his best friend by being stupid.
verbatim_html:
It was amazing how many different ways there were to kill your
best friend by being stupid.

summary_en: Lesath asked if he had been wrong.
verbatim_html:
"I -" Lesath hesitated, then said in a small voice, "I was
wrong, wasn't I?"

summary_en: Harry said Lesath had acted correctly and that he himself was the fool.
verbatim_html:
"You acted exactly as you should have, under the circumstances.
It is I who was a fool."

summary_en: Lesath apologized to his lord.
verbatim_html: "I'm sorry, my lord," whispered Lesath.

summary_en: Harry asked whether Lesath could have killed the troll.
verbatim_html: "If you had come with me, would you have been able to kill the troll?" It wasn't even the correct question, the correct question was whether Harry himself would have considered Lesath as sufficient and flown out sixty seconds earlier, but still...

summary_en: Lesath asked whether he should study the Killing Curse.
verbatim_html:
"I... I'm not sure, my lord... I am not much welcome to duelling
practices in Slytherin, I have not learned the gestures to the
Killing Curse - should I study those arts to better serve you, my
lord?"

summary_en: Harry insisted he was not Lesath's lord.
verbatim_html: "I continue to insist that I am not your lord," Harry said.

summary_en: Lesath replied yes, my lord.
verbatim_html: "Yes, my lord."

summary_en: Harry suggested Lesath learn to defend himself with the Defense Professor's help.
verbatim_html:
"Although," Harry said, "and this is not any kind of order, just
a remark, anyone ought to know how to defend themselves, especially
you. I'm sure the Defense Professor would help you with that on
general principles, if you asked."

summary_en: Lesath bowed and said he would follow Harry's orders.
verbatim_html:
Lesath Lestrange bowed and said, "Yes, my lord, I will follow
your orders if I can, my lord."

summary_en: Harry would have complained about being misunderstood, if he hadn't been understood perfectly.
verbatim_html:
Harry would have complained about being misunderstood, if he
hadn't been understood perfectly.

summary_en: Lesath left.
verbatim_html: Lesath left.

summary_en: Harry stared at the wall.
verbatim_html: Harry stared at the wall.

summary_en: Harry thought he had already figured out all the ways he had been stupid.
verbatim_html:
He'd honestly thought that he'd already figured out all the
different ways that he'd been stupid, after spending half a day
thinking about it.

summary_en: This had just been more overconfidence.
verbatim_html:
Apparently this had just been more overconfidence on his
part.

summary_en: Harry's Slytherin side asked coldly if they understood what they did wrong.
verbatim_html: Do we understand what we did wrong? his Slytherin side said coldly.

summary_en: Harry answered yes.
verbatim_html: Yes, Harry thought.

summary_en: Slytherin said Harry's qualms made no sense and asked why he forgot Lesath.
verbatim_html: Your ethical qualms don't even make sense. You're not tricking Lesath. You did exactly what Lesath thinks you did. You wouldn't have to make excuses for why Lesath was helping you, you could just say you were calling in the debt from rescuing him from bullies, there were six witnesses to that. Hermione died because you forgot about an extremely valuable resource, and you forgot about Lesath because... why?

summary_en: Hufflepuff said having Lesath as a minion seemed Dark-Lordish.
verbatim_html: Because having Lesath Lestrange for a minion seemed sort of Dark-Lordish? Hufflepuff said in a small mental voice. I mean... that decision was probably mostly me...

summary_en: Slytherin radiated contempt and showed an image of Hermione's corpse.
verbatim_html:
Harry's Slytherin side didn't answer that in words, just
radiated contempt and flashed an image of Hermione's corpse.

summary_en: Harry screamed internally to stop it.
verbatim_html: Stop it! Harry screamed internally.

summary_en: Slytherin suggested focusing on efficiency rather than seeming Dark-Lordish.
verbatim_html: Next time, Slytherin said icily, I suggest that we spend more time worrying about what is efficient and effective, and less time worrying about what seems sort of Dark-Lordish.

summary_en: Harry conceded the point.
verbatim_html: Point made, Harry thought, I will.

summary_en: Slytherin said Harry would only listen after his next friend dies.
verbatim_html: No, you won't, said Slytherin. You'll come up with more rationalisations for your petty qualms. You'll start listening to me after your next friend dies.

summary_en: Harry worried he was going insane from the voices in his head.
verbatim_html:
Harry was starting to worry that he was going insane. The
conversations he had with the voices in his head weren't usually
like this.

summary_en: The Boy-Who-Lived.
verbatim_html: The Boy-Who-Lived

summary_en: Pain.
verbatim_html: pain

verbatim_html: Harry Verres trudged on alone

summary_en: Hurts.
verbatim_html: hurts

summary_en: Harry walked on through the silent corridors.
verbatim_html: Harry walked on through the silent corridors.

summary_en: Professor Quirrell demanded to know how Mr. Potter was doing.
verbatim_html: "How is Mr. Potter doing?" demanded Professor Quirrell. There was a tension about the man, you could not quite call it concern, more like an ambusher measuring the time to strike. The Grangers had hardly left with Madam Pomfrey before the Defense Professor had knocked upon the door to her office and then entered without waiting for her answer, and spoken before she could say a word. Part of Minerva wondered distantly whether Harry Potter had picked up that habit from his Defense Professor, being unaware of others' pain when there was something else on his mind, or if it was only a childish flaw which this man had somehow failed to grow out of.

summary_en: McGonagall said Potter had stopped guarding Granger's body and gone to dinner.
verbatim_html: "Mr. Potter has ceased guarding Miss Granger's body," she said, putting some of the chill she felt into her voice. She felt certain that the Defense Professor was not experiencing as much grief as she was, the man had spoken not a single word of Hermione Granger. For him to put demands on her - "I believe he has gone down to dinner."

summary_en: Quirrell demanded to know the boy's state, not physical.
verbatim_html: "I am not asking after the boy's physical state! Have you - has he -" Professor Quirrell made a sharp gesture, as though to indicate a concept for which he had no words.

summary_en: McGonagall said she was about to order Quirrell out of her office.
verbatim_html:
"Not particularly," she said. She was around thirty seconds away
from ordering the Defense Professor out of her office.

summary_en: Quirrell paced and argued that only Lupin might reach Potter now.
verbatim_html:
Professor Quirrell began to pace within the small confines of
her office. "Miss Granger was the only one whose worries he truly
heeded - with her gone - all checks on the boy's recklessness are
removed. I see it now. Who else is there? Mr. Longbottom? Mr.
Potter does not pretend that they are peers. Flitwick? His goblin
blood would only cry for vengeance. Mr. Malfoy, if he were
returned? To what end? Snape? A walking disaster. Dumbledore? Pfah.
Events are already set for catastrophe, they must be steered along
some course they would not naturally go. Who might Mr. Potter heed,
who would not ordinarily speak to him? Cedric Diggory has taught
him, but what would Mr. Diggory say in advice? An unknown. Mr.
Potter spent long in speech with Remus Lupin. To him I have paid
little heed. Would Lupin know the words to speak, the act which
must be done, the sacrifice which must be made to change the boy's
course?" Professor Quirrell whirled on her. "Did Remus Lupin
comfort those in grief or stay those moved to rash deeds, during
his time with the Order of the Phoenix?"

summary_en: McGonagall said Lupin had restrained James Potter in Hogwarts days.
verbatim_html:
"It is not a poor thought," she said slowly. "I believe that Mr.
Lupin was often a voice of restraint to James Potter in his
Hogwarts days."

summary_en: Quirrell said the disaster path must be averted at every point.
verbatim_html: "James Potter," said Professor Quirrell, his eyes narrowing. "The boy is not much like James Potter. Are you confident in the success of this plan? No, that is the wrong question, we are not limited to a single plan. Are you certain that this plan will be enough, that we need essay no others? Asked in such fashion, the question answers itself. The path leading to disaster must be averted along every possible point of intervention." The Defense Professor had resumed pacing the confines of her office, reaching one wall, turning on his heel, pacing to the other.

summary_en: McGonagall told Quirrell she had reached her limits and he should go.
verbatim_html:
"My apologies, Professor," she did not bother keeping the
sharpness from her voice, "but I have quite reached my limits for
the day. You may go."

summary_en: Quirrell said she would be the first he thought of after Granger.
verbatim_html: "You." Professor Quirrell spun, and she found herself gazing directly into eyes of icy blue. "You would be the first one I would think of after Miss Granger, to stay the boy from a folly. Have you already done your utmost? Of course you have not."

summary_en: McGonagall told Quirrell to leave if he had nothing more to say.
verbatim_html: How dare he suggest that. "If you have nothing more to say, Professor, then you will go."

summary_en: Quirrell asked if her confederacy had deduced who he really was.
verbatim_html:
"Has your confederacy deduced who I really am?" The words were
spoken with deceptive mildness.

summary_en: McGonagall said yes, in fact.
verbatim_html: "Yes, in fact. Now -"

summary_en: Pure magic and power crashed into the room.
verbatim_html:
Pure magic, pure power crashed into the room like a flash of
lightning, like a thunderclap echoing about her ears that deafened
her other senses, the papers on her desk blown aside not by any
conjured wind but by the sheer raw force of arcane might.

summary_en: Hermione Granger's death certificates drifted to the floor.
verbatim_html:
Then the power subsided, leaving only Hermione Granger's death
certificates drifting down through the air to the floor.

summary_en: David Monroe warned McGonagall that Potter could become dangerous.
verbatim_html: "I am David Monroe, who fought Voldemort," the man said, still in mild tones. "Heed my words. The boy cannot be allowed to continue in this state of mind. He will become dangerous. It is possible that you have already done everything you can. Yet I find this a very rare event indeed, and more often said than done. I suspect rather that you have only done what you customarily do. I cannot truly comprehend what drives others to break their bounds, since I never had them. People remain surprisingly passive when faced with the prospect of death. Fear of public ridicule or losing one's livelihood is more likely to drive men to extremes and the breaking of their customary habits. On the other side of the war, the Dark Lord had excellent results from the Cruciatus Curse, judiciously used on Marked servants who cannot escape punishment except by success, with no reasonable efforts accepted. Imagine their state of mind within yourself, and ask yourself whether you have truly done all that you can to wrench Harry Potter from his course."

summary_en: McGonagall snapped that he would exercise courtesy in her office.
verbatim_html: "I am a Gryffindor and not much given to being moved by fear," she snapped back. "You will exercise courtesy within my office!"

summary_en: Quirrell said fear moved him and Potter could join rituals inscribed on tombstones.
verbatim_html:
"I find fear an excellent motivation, and indeed it is fear that
moves me now. You-Know-Who, for all his horror, still abided by
certain boundaries. It is my professional judgment, speaking as a
learned wizard almost on par with Dumbledore or
He-Who-Must-Not-Be-Named, that the boy could join the ranks of
those whose rituals are inscribed upon the tombstones of countries.
This is not an idle worry, McGonagall, I have already heard words
to produce the gravest apprehensions."

summary_en: McGonagall said the idea was ridiculous.
verbatim_html:
"Are you mad? You think that Mr. Potter could - this is
ridiculous. Mr. Potter cannot possibly -"

summary_en: A wordless image of a patch of glass on a steel ball crossed her mind.
verbatim_html:
A wordless image crossed her mind of a patch of glass on a steel
ball.

summary_en: McGonagall said Potter would not do such a thing.
verbatim_html: "- Mr. Potter would not do such a thing!"

summary_en: Quirrell said Potter may be reckless once resolved on a goal.
verbatim_html: "His deliberate choice is not required. Wizards rarely set out to invoke their own dooms. Mr. Potter may not strike you as malicious. Does he strike you as reckless once he is resolved upon a goal? I say again that I have specific reason for the gravest possible concerns!"

summary_en: McGonagall asked if Quirrell had spoken to the Headmaster.
verbatim_html:
"Have you spoken to the Headmaster of this?" she said
slowly.

summary_en: Quirrell said Dumbledore could not reach Potter and he would consult Snape.
verbatim_html: "That would be worse than pointless. Dumbledore cannot reach the boy. At best he is wise enough to know this and make things no worse. I lack the requisite frame of mind. You are the one who - but I see that you still look for others to save you." The Defense Professor turned from her, and strode to the door. "I think I shall consult with Severus Snape. The man may be a walking disaster, but he knows the fact, and he may possess a greater understanding of that boy's mood. As for you, madam, imagine yourself at the end of your life, knowing that Britain - but no, Britain is not your true country, is it? Imagine yourself at the end of your life as the darkness eats through the fading walls of Hogwarts, knowing that your students will die with you, remembering this day and realizing there was something else you could have done."
